auditJsDesc: Reads, read-only, how many tasks are enabled in Joomla's Task Scheduler, how many of them are more than an hour past their time and when the newest run was. Joomla runs these tasks only when someone visits the site unless a cron job calls the scheduler, so a quiet site falls behind. Counts and ages only; no task name or setting is read and nothing is changed.
auditJtDesc: Reads, read-only, the table names, sizes and row estimates of the linked MariaDB database and the type, element and folder of every installed Joomla extension, and lists the tables that are not Joomla's own and whose name matches no installed extension. These are candidates, not a verdict: an uninstalled extension may have left them behind, or an installed one may simply name its tables differently. Nothing is dropped or changed; take a backup before cleaning up.
auditJtTables: Tables of extensions that are gone
auditPeDesc: Reads the last 24 hours of the site's runtime container log, read-only, and keeps only what belongs to this site: PHP errors that name a file under the site folder and web server errors for its host name. They are grouped by message with a count, the file and line, and the time of the newest one. Messages are cleaned (passwords, tokens and e-mail addresses are masked) and no stack trace is shown. A log can only show what happened since the container was last created.
auditPerformanceDesc: Requests the public home page and its own stylesheet and script from this computer (read-only GETs): response time of one request, HTML size, whether text is compressed (gzip/br) and whether assets are cached long enough. Works for any stack, including Node and static sites.
auditRhDesc: Reads, read-only, the state of the site's PHP runtime container (running or not, restarts, whether it was stopped for running out of memory, since when it runs), the size of the application log files in the usual places (Laravel, WordPress, Joomla, Symfony and plain error_log files), the age of the active release when the site was deployed with releases, and for a Laravel site the number of waiting and failed queue jobs. No log content and no job data is read; nothing is changed.
auditWordpressDesc: Runs WP-CLI on the server, read-only: pending core update, debug constants and the code editor in wp-config.php, whether XML-RPC is on, how many administrator accounts exist (a count only) and the official checksum check of core and plugin files against wordpress.org. No password, salt or user name leaves the server.
auditWpPerfDesc: Runs WP-CLI on the server, read-only: persistent object cache and page cache, the size of autoloaded options, expired transients, overdue WP-Cron events, the Action Scheduler queue (when the site has one), SAVEQUERIES and the number of active plugins. Only sizes and counts are read; no option name or value leaves the server.
auditWpUpDesc: Reads, read-only, what WordPress already knows about the pending updates (the cached update data; nothing is downloaded and nothing is changed): the new versions, the PHP and WordPress versions they need, the version a plugin was last tested with, major version jumps and a changelog link. Use it before updating everything at once.
auditWpUpPluginsTested: Plugins not tested with this WordPress
changePhpTitle: Migrate to a different PHP runtime
credentialsNote: Save these credentials - the password will not be shown again.
dbUserNote: A dedicated user will be granted access only to this database.
historyEmpty: No history yet. History is saved automatically before each write.
noSitesBefore: No sites configured yet. Make sure FrankenPHP is installed and
siteTypePhpHint: Serves PHP via FrankenPHP. Supports any PHP app.
siteTypeStaticHint: Serves HTML/CSS/JS files only. No PHP, no database needed.
subdomainProxyNote: All traffic to {{domain}} will be forwarded to this address. Use a hostname or IP reachable from the server.
subdomainStaticHint: Files in this directory will be served directly.
subdomainTypePhpHint: Serves PHP via FrankenPHP. Supports WordPress, Laravel, any PHP app.
subdomainTypeProxyHint: Forwards traffic to a local or internal service (e.g. Node.js, Go, Python).
subdomainTypeStaticHint: Serves HTML / CSS / JS files only. No PHP, no database.
envHint: Sets how strict the checks for this site are. Production is the strictest.
envUnconfirmedTitle: Not reviewed yet - treated as production
envReviewTitle: Check the environment of your sites
envReviewBody: Sites that existed before this setting are treated as production. Review them and change the ones that are not.
watchdogHint: Read-only. Recent messages from Drupal's Database Logging, read with Drush. Hostnames, users and request URLs are not shown, and credentials in messages are masked.
watchdogUnavailableNotDrupal: Drupal was not detected at this site root.
watchdogUnavailableMultisiteUnsupported: The log view is not supported on multisite yet.
watchdogUnavailableDrushMissing: Drush is not installed for this site.
watchdogUnavailableCommandUnavailable: Drush cannot show the log. The Database Logging module (dblog) may be off, or Drupal could not start.
watchdogUnavailableBadOutput: Drush answered with something the panel could not read.
joomlaUpdatesHint: Diagnostics only: nothing is installed. Checking runs Joomla's own update check, which refreshes Joomla's update cache and contacts the Joomla update servers.
joomlaUpdatesCoreUnknown: Could not determine the latest version. The update server may be unreachable.
joomlaUpdatesCoreUnreadable: The core check returned nothing the panel could read.
joomlaUpdatesExtensionsUnknown: The extension check returned nothing the panel could read.
joomlaUpdatesExtensionsTruncated: Only the first extensions are listed.
joomlaUpdatesUnavailableNotJoomla: Joomla was not detected at this site root.
joomlaUpdatesUnavailableCliMissing: This site has no Joomla command line (cli/joomla.php), so updates cannot be checked from here. Joomla 4.1 or newer is needed.
joomlaUpdatesUnavailablePhpMissing: The site's runtime has no PHP command line.
joomlaUpdatesUnavailableBadOutput: Joomla answered with something the panel could not read.
auditIntro: These checks request <host>https://{{domain}}</host> from this computer, the way a visitor or a search engine would. Nothing is changed on the site or the server. Environment: <env>{{environment}}</env>.
auditRaDesc: Measures the site folder, read-only: old release directories next to the active release (for sites deployed as a release tree) and rebuildable folders such as node_modules and framework caches. Only sizes and dates are read; nothing is opened, moved or deleted.
auditIndexingDesc: robots.txt, noindex, sitemap, canonical address and http:// resources on the home page.
auditLaravelDesc: Reads the project's files on the server: APP_DEBUG, APP_ENV, whether APP_KEY is set, variables missing compared with .env.example, writable storage folders, the storage link and cached configuration. Only variable names and a few non-secret settings are read; no secret value leaves the server.
auditUploadPhpDesc: Lists PHP files inside upload folders (wp-content/uploads, sites/*/files, images, storage/app/public), where only pictures and documents belong. Only file names are read, never their contents.
auditExposureDesc: Looks for .git, .env, database dumps and archives, phpinfo(), backup copies of wp-config.php, Joomla's configuration.php and Drupal's settings.php, application logs (debug.log, laravel.log, error_log), Composer manifests and open directory listings at common addresses. A file counts only if its content looks like the real thing; the content is never shown or stored.
composerReady: Composer {{version}} is installed on the server and managed by the Operations Engine.
composerNotInstalled: The managed Composer is not installed on this server. Drush and the Composer-based checks need it.
composerEngineUnsupported: The Operations Engine on this server is too old to manage tools. Update the engine, then install Composer.
composerCheckFailed: Composer could not be checked: the Operations Engine did not answer ({{reason}}).
healthNoScore: Not enough data for a score ({{pct}}% of the signals are known)
healthFormula: Weighted mean of the known signals ({{pct}}% of the weight)
drushInstalledHere: Drush is installed in this project.
drushInstallHint: Adds Drush to this project with Composer (composer require drush/drush); the project's composer.json and vendor/ change.
drushAutoStartFailed: Could not start the automatic Drush installation: {{error}}
drushAutoRunning: Installing Drush automatically (Composer first, then Drush). This is done once per site.
drushAutoFailed: The automatic Drush installation on {{when}} failed: {{error}}. It is not retried automatically; use Install Drush to try again.
wpCliInstallHint: Downloads the pinned WP-CLI release to the server and mounts it read-only into the runtime containers; nothing in your sites changes.
drupalActionMaintenanceWarn: Visitors will see the maintenance page.
drupalActionUpdateDbWarn: This applies {{pending}} pending database updates and cannot be undone. Take a fresh database backup first (Backups tab) and consider enabling maintenance mode if the site is live.
cacheClearLaravelDesc: Runs artisan optimize:clear: the compiled, config, route, view and event caches and the application cache store.
cacheClearLaravelWarn: Sessions kept in the cache store are cleared too, so signed-in visitors may be logged out.
maintenanceJoomlaDesc: Takes the site offline with Joomla's own console (site:down) and back online (site:up). Visitors see Joomla's offline page; administrators can still sign in at /administrator.
maintenanceLaravelDesc: Runs artisan down with a one-time bypass token and artisan up to bring the site back. While it is down visitors get a 503 page.
maintenanceEnableWarn: Visitors will no longer see the site until maintenance mode is turned off.
maintenanceUnchanged: The site was already in this mode; nothing was changed.
maintenanceSecretHint: Open your site address followed by this path to see the site while it is down. It is not saved anywhere; turn maintenance mode off and on again to get a new one.
maintenanceSecretIssuedAgain: The bypass token of this request was already shown and cannot be shown again.
appOtlNeedsDrush: Drush is not installed for this site, and the login link is created with it. Use Install Drush in the Drupal section below, then come back.
drupalModAdminUi: Administration UIs enabled (field, views and migrate screens; a finished live site rarely needs them)
drupalModDevelopment: Development helpers enabled (usually not wanted on a live site)
drupalModNone: Nothing stands out among the {{count}} installed modules.
drupalModNotInstalled: In the codebase but not installed (if not needed, remove with Composer after checking that nothing depends on them)
drupalModReviewHint: Read from the module list below. These are candidates to look at, not instructions: nothing is uninstalled or removed from here, and a module that is not listed here may still be unused.
capMissingTool: {{tool}} is not installed for this site.
capMissingToolUnnamed: A required tool is not installed for this site.
capNoDbAccess: No database access for this check.
capMultisiteUnsupported: Multisite is detected, but this action is not supported on multisite yet.
capMissingEngineOpNamed: The server operation {{tool}} is not available yet, so one-time admin login cannot be offered.
capMissingEngineOp: The server operation is not available yet, so one-time admin login cannot be offered.
otlIntro: Log in to the site's admin area without a password, using a single-use link that expires in minutes.
otlLimitTtlFromSite: The lifetime is set by the site (its password reset timeout), not by this panel.
otlLimitSingleUse: Single use is not race-safe: if the link is opened several times at once, each can start a session. Do not share it, and check the site's active sessions if it may have leaked.
otlDialogIntro: This creates a link that logs in as the chosen administrator without a password. The link works once and {{expiry}}. It is shown only once, is not saved anywhere, and anyone who gets it before it is used or expires gets admin access. Do not share it.
otlExpirySite: expires after the time the site itself allows for password reset links (24 hours by default), which this panel cannot shorten
otlDrupalLimits: Drupal does not guarantee single use under simultaneous opens, and the link can stay valid for a long time. Open it yourself right away and do not share it.
otlTruncated: Only the first administrators are listed.
otlSummarySite: Site {{root}}, user {{login}}, valid as long as the site allows.
otlAlreadyIssued: This link was already issued and cannot be shown again. Close this dialog and create a new link.
otlLinkFor: Link for {{login}}. Valid until {{until}} ({{lifetime}}), one use only. It will not be shown again after you close this dialog.
otlClipboardNote: The link is now on your clipboard; clear it when done.
schedulerHint: Laravel runs its scheduled tasks only when a cron job calls php artisan schedule:run every minute. This reads the project's files and the server's crontab; nothing is changed until you add the job.
schedulerConfirm: Add a cron job to the server's crontab that runs php artisan schedule:run every minute, as this site's user, inside its PHP container? You can remove it later in the Cron tab.
auditJoomlaDesc: Reads the site's files on the server: the Joomla version, debug mode, error reporting and Force HTTPS in configuration.php, the file mode of configuration.php, a leftover installation folder and backup or dump files in the site root. Only four non-secret settings are read; no password or secret leaves the server.
auditDbDesc: Reads the size of every table in the database linked to this site (Database tab), read-only: the largest tables, free space that OPTIMIZE TABLE could return, and the tables that usually grow without limit for this application (sessions, logs, caches, queues). Only table names, sizes and row estimates are read; no row content.
auditDrupalDesc: Reads sites/default/settings.php and the file modes on the server: the Drupal version, trusted host patterns, update.php access, error display, whether the configuration and private file folders are inside the web root, and a settings.local.php that is included. Drupal's database password and hash salt are never read out. Needs no Drush; single-site installs only.
auditClDesc: Shows, read-only, which caches sit between a visitor and the code and what each one is doing: the browser, a CDN such as Cloudflare, a cache in front of the site, the CMS page cache, the object cache and PHP OPcache. It fetches the home page twice from this computer and reads the cache settings of the CMS and PHP on the server; nothing is purged or changed. Use it to find the layer to clear when a change does not show.
auditClIngress: Cache in front of the site
auditComposerDesc: Runs composer audit on the project's composer.lock with the server's managed Composer. Package names and versions are sent to Packagist's security advisories service; nothing is installed or changed. In production only the packages that ship with the site are checked. It also counts, from the same lock file, how many of the project's own requirements have a newer release (composer outdated); that line is information only and nothing is updated.
auditPhpCompatDesc: Before you change the PHP version: checks whether the PHP requirements declared by this site's plugins, themes, modules, extensions and Composer packages allow the version you pick. Only declared requirements can be checked. Nothing is changed.
appLogHint: Read-only. The last lines of the application's own log file: Laravel storage/logs, Joomla administrator/logs. Credentials in messages are masked.
appLogLarge: This log is {{size}}. A log that is never rotated keeps growing and can fill the disk; clear it once you are done debugging.
appLogUnavailableNoLogFile: There is no log file yet. Laravel and Joomla create theirs when something is logged.
appLogUnavailableUnreadable: The log file exists but could not be read as the site user.
appLogUnavailableUnsupported: This site has no known log file.
healthListNote: Backups and security headers are not read for the list - open the site for the full score.
extIntro: Everything installed on this site in one list. Read-only: the enabled and update columns show a state only where the source can report it.
extTruncated: The list was cut at the limit; narrow it with the filters.
smokeDesc: A few URLs that must keep working. Run it before and after an update, a clone or a PHP change: the last two runs are compared, so what got worse stands out. Plain requests from this computer; only the status and the time are kept.
smokePathsHint: One path per line, for example /login. At most 20.
joomlaCloneDesc: Copies the files and the database into an existing staging site. The copy gets its own database user and a new secret.
joomlaCloneInfoExisting: If the staging site does not exist yet it is created with the same PHP runtime as the source. An existing staging site has its files and database replaced.
joomlaCloneInfoDb: A new MariaDB database is provisioned with a random password. The copy is checked with Joomla's own console before it is kept; if the check fails the staging site is put back as it was.
joomlaCloneSafetyDesc: Applied to the copy only, never to the original. On by default for staging and development.
joomlaCloneSafety_noindex: Ask search engines not to index it
hardeningOpenTabTitle: Open the tab where this can be fixed
healthListNoteCached: Backups and security headers are from the last time this site was opened - open it to refresh them.
renameChangesServer: On the server: the site's route and runtime config move to the new name, its files move if they live under the default /var/www/<domain> path, and Caddy reloads and asks for a new certificate on the first visit.
renameChangesLocal: In this app: notes, environment label, smoke URLs, deploy settings and history, the auto-deploy cron label, backup job paths under the site's folder, database bindings, and the uptime and WordPress metrics history.
renameChangesValkey: Valkey: the site's Valkey user is renamed from site_{{old}} to site_{{new}}. Its password and database stay the same; change the user name in the site's cache settings.
renameNotChanged: The site's own settings are not edited: a WordPress site address, a Joomla live_site or any URL stored in the database or in config files. DNS for the new domain must point to this server before it can get a certificate. Anything that uses the old domain (webhooks, Cloudflare records, OAuth callbacks) has to be updated by you.
renameValkeyFailed: The Valkey user of the site could not be moved to the new name ({{error}}). The old user site_{{old}} still works; rename it from Valkey > Site access by rotating access for the new domain.
